messages.author: eebf2091d4ee8b1e
messages.subject: Adjust vertically two ggplots
parts:
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
library(gridExtra)

I created two plots with ggplot and want to place them in one figure above each other. Using "grid.arrange" with ncol=1 this is of course possible.
But now my question: The two plots present time series of two parameters for exactly the same period. I want to place the inner plot area (how is this called?) exactly above each other. The y-axis label is in one case two lines and also the two legends (placed on the right side of the plot) differ. Even though the two plots are placed above each other, the inner plot area is not.
I appreciate any help very much!!

Anja

messages.author: fcfcdcef61e0ccd5
messages.subject: Re: Adjust vertically two ggplots
parts:
I would use ggplot2 theme to remove the x-axis labels & ticks from the plot which is supposed to come on top and then set the bottom & top margins of the top and bottom plots respectively to be -0.5 cm or something so that they line up.

Regards
Saurabh

messages.author: e01d780396d5e3f0
messages.subject: Re: Adjust vertically two ggplots
parts:
Hi you could use the following function to align your y axis on both the plots. 


library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
library(gridExtra)
align_plots <- function (...) 
{
  pl <- list(...)
  stopifnot(do.call(all, lapply(pl, inherits, "gg")))
  gl <- lapply(pl, ggplotGrob)
  bind2 <- function(x, y) gtable:::rbind_gtable(x, y, "first")
  combined <- Reduce(bind2, gl[-1], gl[[1]])
  wl <- lapply(gl, "[[", "widths")
  combined$widths <- do.call(grid::unit.pmax, wl)
  grid::grid.newpage()
  grid::grid.draw(combined)
}

To verify, just test with following code: 

align_plots(qplot(1,1),qplot(100,100),qplot(1000,1000)+ylab("two \n lines"))

ps: I found this code on internet some time back but couldn't find it now to give appropriate credit. 

Hope it helps. 

Janesh Devkota
